name: sign_language_methods
query: What architectural approaches exist for continuous sign language recognition?
key_points: Traditional CSLR pipelines use a three-stage architecture: spatial feature extraction, temporal modeling, then sequence alignment (e.g. via CTC or HMM)
AutoSign uses an autoregressive decoder-only transformer to directly translate pose sequences to text, avoiding gloss annotations and alignment mechanisms
MediaPipe and OpenPose are used as landmark/pose detection tools to support real-time recognition
CTC-based alignment methods can overfit and suffer from error propagation

name: curse_of_dimensionality
query: How do neural networks overcome the curse of dimensionality in function approximation?
key_points: Barron's theorem shows neural networks can approximate functions with bounded Fourier moments at a dimension-independent rate of n^(-1/2)
The manifold assumption allows dimension-independent approximation when the target function is supported on a low-dimensional manifold embedded in high-dimensional space
PDE-based structural assumptions are an alternative route to avoiding the curse of dimensionality, in contrast to classical numerical methods like finite elements which still suffer from it

name: quantum_error_correction
query: What approaches exist for fault-tolerant quantum error correction and decoding?
key_points: Transversal algorithmic fault tolerance allows fault-tolerant logical operations to be performed with only a constant number of syndrome extraction rounds, instead of scaling with the code distance

The Sparse Mamba Decoder processes only the active defect/detection events in a syndrome (a small fraction of the total) using a Mamba state-space backbone, achieving lower complexity than dense decoders that process the full syndrome array
Classical and quantum error correction share the same basic principle of adding redundancy to protect information against noise, though quantum channels behave differently from classical ones
Concatenated codes are a construction used for fault-tolerant quantum computation

name: sign_language_deep_learning
query: What recent deep learning approaches improve sign language recognition and generation?
key_points: AutoSign uses an autoregressive decoder-only transformer to directly translate pose sequences to text, avoiding gloss annotations and alignment mechanisms
A multimodal sign language pre-training framework combines sign-text contrastive learning with masked pose modeling, trained on a large-scale dataset of about 1.5 million samples
CSF enables direct multilingual-to-sign-language translation without using English as an intermediary, using a nine-slot semantic schema

name: deep_learning_theory_pair
query: What theoretical limitations and advances exist in modern deep learning models?
key_points: Barron's theorem shows neural networks can approximate functions with bounded Fourier moments at a dimension-independent rate of n^(-1/2)

Existing evidential deep learning models suffer from a fundamental limitation: their activation functions create zero-evidence regions that prevent the model from learning from training samples that fall into them
A regularized evidential model (RED) with a positive-evidence regularizer is proposed to address the zero-evidence-region learning deficiency
